subject: Animation
title: The Nine Old Men of Disney
description: Learn The Nine Old Men of Disney in one minute.

hook.text: Disney's core animators were called the Nine Old Men — they defined the look and feel of animated storytelling.

buildup.text: Artists like Frank Thomas, Ollie Johnston, and Milt Kahl created characters with unprecedented emotional range.

discovery.text: They codified the twelve principles of animation — rules that every animator in the world still learns.

twist.text: Despite creating Disney's greatest works, most of the Nine Old Men remained unknown to the general public.

climax.text: The Nine Old Men built the artistic foundation that Disney animation still stands on today.

punchline.text: Nine unknown artists wrote the rules every animator follows.

quiz.question: What lasting contribution did Disney's Nine Old Men make?
options: They codified the twelve principles of animation that every animator worldwide still learns
They directed all Disney theme parks

details.summary: Disney's Nine Old Men were the core animators who defined the Disney style from Snow White through The Jungle Book. Their collective expertise, codified in animation's twelve principles, became the foundation of character animation worldwide.
details.whyItMatters: The Nine Old Men established character animation principles that are still taught in every animation school. Their work defined how animated characters move, express emotion, and connect with audiences for all time.
takeaways: The Nine Old Men were Disney's core creative team for three decades
They codified the twelve principles of animation still used universally today
Their collective work defined the Disney style of character animation

faq.question: Who were the Nine Old Men of Disney?
faq.answer: Les Clark, Marc Davis, Ollie Johnston, Milt Kahl, Ward Kimball, Eric Larson, John Lounsbery, Wolfgang Reitherman, and Frank Thomas. Walt Disney nicknamed them after FDR's description of the Supreme Court justices.

faq.question: What are the twelve principles of animation?
faq.answer: Squash and stretch, anticipation, staging, straight-ahead vs pose-to-pose, follow through, slow in/slow out, arcs, secondary action, timing, exaggeration, solid drawing, and appeal. These principles remain the foundation of all character animation.
